content.thinking:
The experiment completed successfully. Let me extract the results:

Overall SR: 42.6% (213/500)

Per-task results:
1. put both the alphabet soup and the tomato sauce in the basket: 64.0% (32/50)
2. put both the cream cheese box and the butter in the basket: 60.0% (30/50)
3. turn on the stove and put the moka pot on it: 54.0% (27/50)
4. put the black bowl in the bottom drawer of the cabinet and close it: 34.0% (17/50)


5. put the white mug on the left plate and put the yellow and white mug on the right plate: 38.0% (19/50)
6. pick up the book and place it in the back compartment of the caddy: 70.0% (35/50)
7. put the white mug on the plate and put the chocolate pudding to the right of the plate: 26.0% (13/50)
8. put both the alphabet soup and the cream cheese box in the basket: 50.0% (25/50)
9. put both moka pots on the stove: 14.0% (7/50)
10. put the yellow and white mug in the microwave and close it: 16.0% (8/50)

The remaining tasks show quite a bit of variation in performance, with the book placement task performing best at 70% and the dual moka pot task struggling significantly at just 14%. The experiment ran for about 648 minutes total.

Looking at the different attention mechanisms, the baseline achieved 52.8% accuracy, while the attention-based approach with k=0.95 dropped to 49.8%. The L2 norm variants performed worse across the board, with k=0.95 reaching 42.6% and k=0.9 at 43.6%. Interestingly, keeping more tokens with k=0.95 actually hurt performance compared to k=0.9, which is a small but notable 1% difference.
